doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: The elders as pioneers and freedom fighters
summary: She reflects on the honor of helping the pioneers who were kings and queens in Europe but faced racism at home.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: privilege of makes me tearful, you know, to think about who these people were. These were the pioneers of the music. These were the original freedom fighters. These were the people who found a way out of the racism because in Europe these people, in America you know you’re talking about the amount of racism we had while they were in the height of their careers, and in Europe they were kings and queens. These were brilliant people who recreated an entire and reinvented an existence for them where they got to be acknowledged for who they truly are and the beauty they contributed to this world you know. I’m sorry, go ahead.
